title: Feature Flag Governance and Rollout Playbook
author: Maya Liang
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's conventions, ownership, and operational procedures for feature flags used across the platform (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane and Console). It focuses on safety, auditability, and fast recovery to keep customer-facing services within SLOs during rollouts.

Scope:
- Applies to all runtime, API, console, and infra-facing feature flags (server-side toggles and rollout configuration stored in the feature-flag service).
- Does NOT cover client-side feature flags embedded in browser SDKs (see frontend-flagging-guide).

Goals:
- Ensure consistent naming, lifecycle, testing, monitoring, and rollback mechanics for every flag.
- Provide clear ownership and decision gates for risky or customer-impacting flags.
- Minimize blast radius with progressive rollouts and automatic safety gates.

Key definitions:
- Flag owner: individual responsible for the flag while active (creates the flag, writes tests, monitors rollout).
- Flag steward: platform team member responsible for flag lifecycle policies and audits.
- Canary: small percentage rollout to verify basic behavior.

Roles & Ownership:
- Feature flag creator (engineering/product): proposes, implements flag, writes unit/integration tests, and owns initial rollout.
- Flag reviewer (peer): approves naming, safety gates, and test coverage in PR.
- Release manager (platform ops): approves production rollout windows and coordinates with SRE if required.
- Flag steward (platform): runs monthly audits and maintains flag registry.

Naming conventions (required):
Use this ASCII table for quick reference:

| Prefix | Description | Examples |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| ff.feature. | Behavioral or UX feature flags | ff.feature.persist-kv-cache |
| ff.experiment. | A/B experiments and user-variant flags | ff.experiment.rank-v2 |
| ff.unsafe. | High-risk flags that require SRE approval | ff.unsafe.kv-shard-remap |
| ff.rollout. | Rollout strategy definitions (percent, cohorts) | ff.rollout.prompt-prefetch |

Flag metadata requirements (in flag registry entry):
- description: short intent and expected behavior (1–2 sentences).
- owner: GitHub handle and pager.
- risk_level: low|medium|high. High must include SRE approver.
- rollout_plan: percentages, target cohorts, burn-in window.
- kill_switch: documented immediate revert path.

Safe default policy:
- All flags default to "off" unless explicitly scoped to a safe experiment cohort.
- High-risk flags must require a secondary approval in PRs and a scheduled rollout window.

Pre-rollout checks (automated & manual):
1) Code-level: unit tests, integration tests exercising both on/off paths, lint pass.
2) CI smoke: e2e smoke with default off and a test cohort on.
3) Canary plan: define metrics and acceptance criteria (latency, error-rate, CPU).
4) Rollout approval: release manager sign-off for high-risk.

Rollout procedure (step-by-step):
1. Create flag in the feature-flag service using the standard CLI or API. Record metadata in the registry.
   - Example CLI: redwood-ff create --name ff.feature.new-cache --owner maya.liang --desc "Enable KV prefetch for L1 cache" --risk low
2. Deploy code behind flag to staging with default OFF. Run integration tests.
3. Canary: target 1% of internal traffic (team cohort) for 1 hour. Observe metrics.
4. Progressive ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Each step requires a minimum observation period: low risk 15m, medium 30m, high 60m.
5. If any safety gate trips, execute rollback procedure (see "Kill switch and rollback").

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Service error rate (5xx) increase <= +0.05% absolute and <= 10% relative vs baseline.
- Median p95 latency change <= +25ms.
- CPU/GPU utilization increase <= +8% sustained per node.

Kill switch and rollback (fast-path):
1) Use the feature-flag control plane UI or API to immediately set flag to OFF for all cohorts.
   - API example: curl -X POST https://ff-api.redwood.internal/v1/flags/ff.feature.new-cache/toggle -d '{"state":"off"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN"
2) If flag toggle fails or downstream state persists, scale affected service replica count to 0/replace pods as a last resort, following SRE coordination.
3) Open an incident channel (#platform-incident) and tag SRE and the original owner. Document time, actions, and telemetry snapshot.

Monitoring and dashboards (what to watch):
- Flag-specific dashboard card: rollout percentage, user-cohort counts, success_ratio, errors/sec, p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU per-pod.
- Cross-service SLO delta panel: compare baseline SLO windows to current.
- Alerting: create short-lived rollout alerts for the duration of the ramp. Example thresholds (temporary alerts):
  - ff.rollout.error-rate-high: error_rate_change > 0.1% for 3m -> Pager to SRE and owner.
  - ff.rollout.latency-regression: p95_increase > 50ms for 5m -> page owner only.

Example dashboard query snippets (PromQL):
- error rate delta: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-server\", code=~\"5..\", flag=~\"ff.feature.new-cache\"}[1m])) by (instance)) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-server\", flag!~\"ff.feature.new-cache\"}[1m])) by (instance)

Audit, retention & cleanup:
- Flags older than 90 days in ON state must have an audit entry explaining ongoing need.
- Stale flags (not toggled or referenced for 180 days) will be listed for deletion in the monthly steward review.
- Flag registry keeps a change log with actor and timestamp for 365 days.

Postmortem and retrospective triggers:
- Any rollout that causes a P1 incident or SLO breach requires a postmortem with RCA and follow-ups.
- Minor incidents (brief rollbacks with no customer impact) should be recorded in the monthly platform retrospective.

Runbook snippets (quick commands):
- Toggle flag (CLI): redwood-ff toggle ff.feature.<name> --state off --reason "rollout regression"
- Check cohorts: redwood-ff inspect ff.feature.<name> --format json | jq '.cohorts'
- List recent changes: redwood-ff history --name ff.feature.<name> --limit 25

Escalation matrix (summary):
- 0-5 minutes: Flag owner attempts immediate toggle. Notify #platform-incident.
- 5-20 minutes: Platform on-call (pager) engages, SRE joins if there are signs of cluster-level impact.
- >20 minutes: Declare incident P1, invoke incident response runbook, consider rollback and rollback mitigation plans (DB migrations, long-running jobs).

Versioning & deployments to control plane:
- Flag control plane schema changes must be backwards compatible. Any migration requires a migration plan and a canary.

Operational improvements & roadmap items:
- Q1 2026: Implement automated canary analysis (auto-rollback if metric divergence exceeds threshold).
- Q2 2026: Add cohort-aware distributed tracing to tie user cohorts to request traces.
- Ongoing: tighter CI hooks to require registry metadata in PRs for any code that introduces flags.

Appendix: Example flag registry JSON template (stored in the registry UI):
{
  "name": "ff.feature.new-cache",
  "description": "Enable L1 KV prefetch for short-lived tokens",
  "owner": "maya.liang@redwood.ai",
  "risk_level": "low",
  "rollout_plan": "1% internal -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%",
  "kill_switch": "redwood-ff toggle ff.feature.new-cache --state off"
}
